one_sentence_story: In 1989, Leda Cosmides (with John Tooby) proved that humans fail abstract 'If P then Q' logic ~80% of the time yet leap to ~75% accuracy on unfamiliar rules ('cassava root to facial tattoo') the instant they involve catching a Social-Contract Cheater who took a rationed benefit without paying the cost.
so_what_for_you: Translate dry abstract policies, study formulas, and team agreements into concrete **'Benefit Received Contribution Owed'** terms so everyone's 75% intuitive radar switches on — and remember our hairline free-rider alarm can over-fire on honest misunderstandings.

jargon_map.plain: specialized reasoning procedure ('If you take Benefit B, you must satisfy Requirement R') tuned to check Benefit-Taken ('Cassava') and Cost-Not-Paid ('No Tattoo')
jargon_map.analogy: a mental turnstile checking who hopped the gate without a ticket

jargon_map.plain: proving 75% accuracy works on a rule no participant ever lived through in real life — ruling out simple rote memory
jargon_map.analogy: aceing a free-rider test on an imaginary island

jargon_map.plain: flipping not-P and Q (~71%) instead of formal logic's P and not-Q when the phrasing reverses ('If you pay Cost, you get Benefit')
jargon_map.analogy: following the free lunch instead of following the 'If-Then' grammar

jargon_map.plain: selective impairment on social-cheater cards (39%) despite preserved hazard-precaution cards (70%) after orbitofrontal + amygdala damage
jargon_map.analogy: two separate circuit breakers inside identical 4-card puzzles
